newsitem.title: USA: World Airways July flying levels up 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: World Airways July flying levels up 23 pct.

text.p: World Airways Inc said Friday block hours flown for continuing operations totaled 3,940 for July 1997, up 23 percent from 3,209 for July 1996.
The company said the increase resulted primarily from the shift in the mix of business from scheduled service operations in 1996 to wet lease operations in 1997.
Average daily utilization was 9.9 block hours per day compared with 9.6 block hours per day for the same period in 1996.
Average aircraft units were 12.9 compared with 10.8 in July 1996.

For the year to date period, block hours flown for continuing operations were 28,090 versus 25,215 for the same period a year ago, which is an 11 percent increase. Average daily utilization was 9.8 block hours per day versus 9.9 block hours per day for the same period a year ago.
Average aircraft units were 13.5 compared with 11.9 for the same period in 1996.
World Airways is 62 percent owned by WorldCorp, 18 percent by MHS Berhad of Malaysia and 20 percent by public investors.
